Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: Who is Elisiv of Kyiv's spouse?
Document 1: In the midst of the 11th century, when the Viking Age was slowly giving way to the dawn of a new era, two powerful figures emerged in the realms of Norway and Kyiv. Elisiv, a princess of Kyiv, and Harald III, the King of Norway, would soon find their lives intertwined in a union that would shape the course of history. As she matured, her beauty and intelligence caught the attention of suitors from across the continent. Meanwhile, in Norway, Harald III, also known as Harald Hardrada, had risen to power through a series of military campaigns and strategic alliances. His reputation as a fierce warrior and cunning leader had earned him the respect and fear of his contemporaries. As he consolidated his power, Harald set his sights on securing a marriage that would cement his position and expand his influence. It was against this backdrop that the paths of Elisiv and Harald converged. The exact circumstances of their meeting are lost to the annals of time, but historians agree that the two were married in the early 1040s. The union was a calculated move, designed to strengthen the bonds between Norway and Kyiv, and to secure a powerful ally in the region. One of the earliest recorded references to Elisiv's marriage to Harald can be found in the Icelandic Sagas, medieval texts that chronicle the history of the Viking Age. The Saga of Harald Hardrada, written in the 13th century, explicitly states that Harald married Elisiv, the daughter of Yaroslav of Kyiv. This account is corroborated by the Russian Primary Chronicle, a contemporaneous source that confirms Elisiv's parentage and her marriage to the Norwegian king. Further evidence of the marriage can be gleaned from the archaeological record. Excavations at the Viking Age settlement of Kaupang, in southern Norway, have uncovered artifacts that suggest a strong cultural exchange between Norway and Kyiv during the 11th century. The presence of Eastern European ceramics and jewelry, alongside Norse artifacts, points to a period of intense cultural and economic exchange, which would have been facilitated by the marriage of Elisiv and Harald.
Document 2: As the sun dipped below the rolling hills of Kyiv, Elisiv, the Norwegian royal consort, strolled through the grand halls of the palace, her silk gown rustling with each step. The air was alive with the whispers of courtiers and the soft clinking of silverware, a testament to the evening's festivities. Tonight, the palace would play host to a gathering of nobles and dignitaries from across the realm, all vying for the favor of the monarch. As Elisiv turned a corner, her gaze fell upon a tall, dark-haired figure standing by the window, his piercing blue eyes fixed on the stars twinkling outside. There was something about his quiet confidence, his air of authority, that drew her in. She felt an inexplicable sense of familiarity, as if she had known him all her life. "Lord Walker," she said, her voice barely above a whisper, as she approached him. Jonathan R. R. Walker, the peerage person of note, turned to face her, a hint of a smile playing on his lips. "Your Highness," he replied, his deep voice sending a shiver down her spine. As they exchanged pleasantries, Elisiv couldn't help but notice the way Walker's eyes crinkled at the corners, the way his smile seemed to hold a secret only she was privy to. It was as if they shared a connection, a bond that went beyond mere acquaintances. The evening wore on, with Elisiv and Walker finding themselves drawn together time and again, their conversations flowing effortlessly from politics to literature to the intricacies of court life. It was as if they had known each other for years, not mere hours. As the night drew to a close, Elisiv felt a pang of disappointment. She didn't want the evening to end, didn't want to leave Walker's side. And yet, as she bid him farewell, she couldn't shake the feeling that their connection was more than just a chance encounter. It was as if fate had brought them together, had woven their lives into a tapestry of love and loyalty.
